en: a spot right beneath one's chin; immediate vicinity

examples.en: It was cold, so I pulled my scarf up to just under my chin.

examples.ko: 아기가 제 턱밑에서 새근새근 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is sleeping soundly right under my chin.
I nicked the area under my chin while shaving.
The water rose up to my chin, and I was so scared.
The deadline is already right on top of us.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 우리 집 턱밑에 있어서 자주 가요.
examples.en: That shop is right next to my house, so I go often.

explain: 몸에서는 턱 바로 아래 부분을 말하고, 비유로 '아주 가까운 곳'이라는 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 보통 '턱밑까지', '턱밑에'처럼 조사와 함께 나와요. 가까운 거리를 강조하고 싶을 때 '바로 앞'보다 더 급박한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The second-place team has closed in right behind the first-place team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경쟁 상대가 바로 뒤까지 가까이 따라왔다는 뜻으로, 곧 따라잡힐 것 같은 긴장감이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a rival has come right up behind you, with a feeling that you may be caught soon.

explain_en: For the body it means the area just below the chin, and figuratively it often gives a sense of 'very close by'. It usually appears with particles, like '턱밑까지' or '턱밑에'. When you want to stress closeness, it feels more urgent than '바로 앞'.

examples.ko: 그가 말할 때마다 턱뼈가 움직이는 게 보여요.
examples.en: I can see his jawbone move every time he talks.
I badly injured my jawbone when I fell.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 턱뼈 사진을 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me an X-ray of my jawbone.
They say the jawbone where the tooth was pulled has weakened.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 턱뼈가 각져서 인상이 강해 보여요.
examples.en: That actor has an angular jawbone, so he looks strong-featured.
I saw a fossil of an animal's jawbone at the museum.

explain: 몸의 '턱'은 얼굴 아랫부분 전체를 말하고, '턱뼈'는 그 안의 뼈를 가리켜요. 병원이나 치과에서 자주 들을 수 있어요. 사람 얼굴의 윤곽을 말할 때는 '턱선'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '턱' is the whole lower part of the face, and '턱뼈' points to the bone inside it. You often hear it at hospitals and dentists. When talking about the outline of a face, people also say '턱선'.

examples.en: My father is growing a beard these days.
His beard was so long that I didn't recognize him at first.
Grandfather's white beard looks really cool.
My beard tends to grow fast.
That man trimmed his beard neatly.

examples.ko: 동생이 붙임 턱수염을 달고 산타 흉내를 냈어요.
examples.en: My little brother put on a fake beard and imitated Santa.

explain: '턱수염'은 턱에 난 수염이고, 입 위의 수염은 '콧수염', 볼 쪽은 '구레나룻'이라고 해요. 수염을 통틀어 말할 때는 그냥 '수염'이라고 해요. 수염을 '기르다', '깎다', '다듬다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: '턱수염' is hair on the chin; a mustache is '콧수염' and sideburns are '구레나룻'. For facial hair in general, people just say '수염'. It goes with verbs like '기르다' (grow), '깎다' (shave) and '다듬다' (trim).

examples.en: That bearded man is famous in the neighborhood.
My uncle's nickname is 'Hairy'.
The hairy guy smiled and opened the door for me.
A bearded pirate appeared in the movie, and it was scary.
After growing his beard, he became a total hairy guy.

examples.ko: 털보 사장님이 만든 빵이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The bread made by the bearded boss is the tastiest.

explain: 수염이나 몸에 털이 많은 사람을 편하게 부르는 말이에요. 친근한 별명처럼 쓸 수도 있지만 모르는 사람에게 직접 말하면 실례일 수 있어요. 주로 남자에게 써요.
explain_en: It is a casual word for a man with a lot of beard or body hair. It can be a friendly nickname, but saying it straight to a stranger can be rude. It is mostly used for men.

examples.en: My younger sister knitted a scarf with wool yarn.
Grandmother is knitting with wool yarn.

examples.ko: 문구점에서 빨간 털실을 두 뭉치 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two balls of red yarn at the stationery store.
The cat is playing with a ball of yarn.
The yarn is tangled, and it's really hard to untangle.
My head feels warm when I wear a yarn hat.

explain: 뜨개질에 쓰는 양털 같은 실이고, 보통 '털실로 짜다/뜨다'처럼 말해요. 실 한 덩어리는 '뭉치'나 '타래'로 세어요. 일상에서는 그냥 '실'이라고 하기도 하지만 털로 만든 실은 '털실'이라고 해야 정확해요.
explain_en: This is wool-like yarn used for knitting, and people say '털실로 짜다/뜨다'. One lump of it is counted as a '뭉치' or '타래'. In daily talk people may just say '실', but yarn made of wool is precisely '털실'.

examples.en: It's vacation, so the classroom is totally empty.
It's the end of the month, so my wallet is totally empty.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 식당이 텅텅 비어요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the restaurant is totally empty.

examples.ko: 냉장고가 텅텅 비어서 장을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: The fridge is completely empty, so I have to go grocery shopping.
I was surprised that the parking lot was totally empty.
There were no customers, so the shop was totally empty.

explain: 거의 항상 '비다'와 함께 써서 '아무것도 없이 완전히 비어 있다'는 느낌을 줘요. '텅 비다'처럼 '텅'만 쓸 때보다 비어 있는 정도를 더 강조해요. 사람이 없는 장소와 돈이 없는 지갑에 모두 써요.
explain_en: It almost always goes with '비다' and gives the feeling of being completely empty. It stresses the emptiness more than '텅' alone, as in '텅 비다'. It is used both for places with no people and for wallets with no money.

examples.en: Mom pats the crying baby's back.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 어깨를 토닥이며 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend comforted me by patting my shoulder.
I slowly patted the child's chest to put him to sleep.
Please pat my back and tell me it's okay.
The teacher patted my head and walked by.

examples.ko: 수고했다고 서로 어깨를 토닥이는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see them patting each other's shoulders to say 'good job.'

explain: 손으로 부드럽게 가볍게 두드린다는 느낌이고, 위로하거나 달래거나 칭찬할 때 많이 써요. 세게 치는 '때리다'와는 달리 따뜻한 마음이 담겨 있어요. 보통 등, 어깨, 머리처럼 몸에 쓰고 '토닥토닥'이라는 흉내말도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It carries a feel of gently tapping with the hand, and is often used to comfort, soothe or praise someone. Unlike '때리다' (hit), it carries warmth. It is usually used on the back, shoulder or head, and the sound word '토닥토닥' is also common.

examples.en: My little brother sulked because his toy was taken away.

examples.ko: 여자 친구가 토라져서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My girlfriend is sulking and won't talk to me.
The child went into the room with a sulky face.

examples.ko: 별것도 아닌 일로 왜 자꾸 토라져요?
examples.en: Why do you keep sulking over nothing?

examples.ko: 친구가 토라진 것 같아서 먼저 사과했어요.
examples.en: My friend seemed upset, so I apologized first.
Don't sulk. Tell me the reason.

explain: 서운하거나 마음이 상해서 말을 안 하거나 표정을 굳히는 모습이에요. 화를 크게 내는 '화나다'와 달리 조용히 삐치는 느낌이고, 가까운 사이에서 많이 써요. 비슷한 '삐치다'는 더 구어체예요.
explain_en: It describes going quiet or stiff-faced because you feel hurt or let down. Unlike '화나다', which is open anger, it feels like quietly sulking and is used between close people. The similar '삐치다' is more colloquial.

examples.en: My grandmother in the countryside sent me native honey.
Native honey is more expensive than regular honey.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸렸을 때 토종꿀을 따뜻한 물에 타 마셔요.
examples.en: When I have a cold, I mix native honey into warm water and drink it.

examples.ko: 이 토종꿀은 맛이 진하고 향이 좋아요.
examples.en: This native honey has a rich taste and a nice scent.
They say it's native honey collected directly in the mountains.
I bought a jar of native honey as a gift.

explain: '토종'은 그 땅에서 오래 자란 원래 품종이라는 뜻이라 '토종꿀'은 한국 토종벌이 만든 꿀을 말해요. 보통 양봉 꿀보다 귀하고 비싸다고 생각해서 선물로도 많이 줘요. 반대로 외국에서 들어온 종류는 '외래종'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '토종' refers to an original breed long native to the land, so '토종꿀' is honey made by native Korean bees. It is generally seen as rarer and pricier than farmed honey and is often given as a gift. The opposite, a species brought from abroad, is '외래종'.

examples.en: On the weekend I ate boiled native chicken soup with my family.
Native chicken has chewier meat than regular chicken.
This restaurant is famous because it only uses native chicken.

examples.ko: 시골에서 토종닭을 마당에 키우는 집이 많아요.
examples.en: In the countryside, many houses raise native chickens in the yard.
These are eggs laid by native chickens, so they taste rich.

examples.ko: 여름 보양식으로 토종닭을 푹 고아 먹어요.
examples.en: As a summer health food, I slowly simmer native chicken and eat it.

explain: 우리나라에서 오래 키워 온 닭 품종을 말하고, 식당에서는 '토종닭 백숙'이나 '토종닭 닭볶음탕'처럼 메뉴 이름에 자주 나와요. 일반 닭보다 고기가 쫄깃하다고 해서 오래 끓이는 요리에 많이 써요. 값도 조금 더 비싸요.
explain_en: It refers to chicken breeds raised in Korea for a long time and often appears on menus like '토종닭 백숙' or '토종닭 닭볶음탕'. The meat is said to be chewier than regular chicken, so it is often used in long-simmered dishes. It also costs a bit more.

examples.ko: 톱날이 무뎌서 나무가 잘 안 잘려요.
examples.en: The saw blade is dull, so the wood doesn't cut well.
Be careful not to cut your hand on the saw blade.
I bought a new saw blade at the hardware store.
My father sharpened the saw blade and used it again.
The saw blade spun fast, and it was scary.

examples.ko: 이 칼은 톱날 모양이라 빵이 잘 썰려요.
examples.en: This knife has a serrated edge, so it cuts bread well.

explain: 톱에서 이가 나 있는 날 부분을 말해요. '칼날', '가위날'처럼 도구의 날카로운 부분은 '-날'로 말해요. 빵칼처럼 톱니 모양의 날은 '톱날 모양'이라고 설명하기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the toothed cutting part of a saw. For tools, the sharp part is named with '-날', as in '칼날' (knife blade) and '가위날' (scissor blade). A bread knife's serrated edge can be described as '톱날 모양'.

examples.en: My father saws wood in the yard.
I almost hurt my hand while sawing.

examples.ko: 나무를 반듯하게 톱질하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to saw wood straight.
Please put on gloves and saw it.
The carpenter quickly sawed the board.

examples.ko: 주말마다 아버지와 같이 톱질하며 의자를 만들어요.
examples.en: Every weekend I make a chair with my father, sawing together.

explain: 톱으로 나무 같은 것을 자르는 동작이에요. 일상에서는 '톱으로 자르다'라고도 많이 말하지만 '톱질하다'는 톱을 앞뒤로 움직이는 동작 자체에 초점이 있어요. '톱질을 하다'처럼 명사 '톱질'과 '하다'를 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the action of cutting something such as wood with a saw. In daily talk people also say '톱으로 자르다', but '톱질하다' focuses on the back-and-forth motion of sawing itself. It can also be split as the noun '톱질' plus '하다', as in '톱질을 하다'.

examples.en: We analyzed the survey results using statistical methods.
This difference has no statistical significance.

examples.ko: 통계적 자료를 보면 인구가 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: According to the statistical data, the population is decreasing.

examples.ko: 통계적으로 겨울에 감기 환자가 더 많아요.
examples.en: Statistically, there are more cold patients in winter.
That result is statistically reliable.

examples.ko: 통계적 관점에서 보면 조금 다른 이야기가 돼요.
examples.en: From a statistical point of view, it becomes a slightly different story.

explain: '통계적 방법/자료/의미'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 쓰고, '통계적으로'는 부사처럼 써요. '통계'는 숫자를 모아서 정리한 것이라 뉴스나 발표, 논문에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '데이터를 보면'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is placed before a noun, as in '통계적 방법/자료/의미', and '통계적으로' works like an adverb. Since '통계' means numbers gathered and organized, it appears often in news, presentations and papers. In everyday talk people also say '데이터를 보면'.

examples.en: Please apply following the usual procedure.
Delivery usually takes about two days.
This price is about the normal level.
Meetings are normally held in the morning.

examples.ko: 그건 통상적 방법으로는 해결이 안 돼요.
examples.en: That can't be solved by ordinary methods.
Students usually take exams on Monday.

explain: '보통', '일반적'과 비슷하지만 더 딱딱해서 공지, 뉴스, 서류에서 많이 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '보통'이나 '원래'를 더 자주 말해요. '통상적 절차'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰거나 '통상적으로'를 부사처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '보통' and '일반적' but stiffer, so you see it in notices, news and documents. In daily conversation, people say '보통' or '원래' more often. Use it before a noun like '통상적 절차', or as an adverb with '통상적으로'.

en: single large pane of glass; full glass wall

examples.ko: 이 카페는 통유리라서 밖이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: This café has full glass walls, so you can see outside well.

examples.ko: 거실에 통유리 창이 있어서 햇빛이 많이 들어와요.
examples.en: The living room has a big glass window, so a lot of sunlight comes in.

examples.ko: 통유리 너머로 눈 오는 풍경을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I watched the snowy scenery through the big glass window.

examples.ko: 통유리는 겨울에 좀 추울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Full glass walls can be a bit cold in winter.

examples.ko: 새 건물은 앞면이 전부 통유리로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The new building's front is entirely made of large single sheets of glass.

examples.ko: 통유리에 새가 부딪히지 않게 스티커를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put stickers on the big glass window so birds won't hit it.

explain: 창틀로 나누지 않고 한 장으로 크게 만든 유리를 말해요. 카페나 새 건물, 거실 창에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 안이 밝고 전망이 좋다는 좋은 느낌으로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to one large sheet of glass that isn't divided by a frame. The word is common for cafés, new buildings and living room windows. People often use it with a positive feel of brightness and a good view.

examples.en: I received my report card at school today.

examples.ko: 통지표에 선생님이 좋은 말을 써 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher wrote kind words on my report card.
I'm afraid to show my report card to Mom.
The report card comes home before vacation.
My grades on the report card went up from last semester.

examples.ko: 제 통지표를 보고 부모님이 칭찬해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents praised me after looking at my report card.

explain: 학교에서 한 학기가 끝날 때 성적과 생활 모습을 적어 집에 보내는 종이예요. 보통 '통지표를 받다/보내다'라고 말해요. 초등학교와 중학교에서 많이 쓰고, 고등학교나 대학교에서는 '성적표'라고 더 자주 해요.
explain_en: This is the paper a school sends home at the end of a term, listing grades and school life. People usually say '통지표를 받다/보내다'. It is common for elementary and middle school, while for high school and university people more often say '성적표'.

examples.en: This road is closed to traffic because of construction.
A no-passage sign is posted at the entrance.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 산길은 통행금지가 됐어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the mountain road was closed.
I heard that in the old days there was a curfew every night.
You must not enter the restricted area.

examples.ko: 차량 통행금지라서 걸어서 갈 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Cars are banned, so we have no choice but to walk.

explain: 길이나 구역으로 사람이나 차가 지나가지 못하게 막는다는 뜻으로, 표지판이나 안내문에서 많이 봐요. '차량 통행금지', '보행자 통행금지'처럼 대상을 앞에 붙여요. 옛날 한국에는 밤에 돌아다닐 수 없던 '야간 통행금지'도 있었어요.
explain_en: It means people or vehicles may not pass through a road or area, and you often see it on signs and notices. You put the target in front, as in '차량 통행금지' or '보행자 통행금지'. In Korea's past there was also a nighttime curfew called '야간 통행금지'.

examples.ko: 기숙사는 규칙을 어긴 사람에게 퇴실을 요구할 권한이 있어요.
examples.en: The dorm has the authority to ask rule-breakers to leave.

examples.ko: 독서실에서는 입실 시간과 퇴실 시간을 꼭 기록해야 해요.
examples.en: At the study room you must write down your entry and exit times.
Hotels usually require you to check out by 11 a.m.
I plan to check out this afternoon.

examples.ko: 퇴실하기 전에 방을 깨끗이 정리해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tidy up the room before you leave.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝난 사람은 먼저 퇴실해도 돼요.
examples.en: People who have finished the exam may leave the room first.

explain: 독서실, 기숙사, 호텔, 시험장처럼 정해진 방에서 나올 때 쓰는 말이고, 반대말은 '입실하다'예요. 호텔에서는 '체크아웃하다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 병원에서 나올 때는 '퇴원하다'를 써요.
explain_en: This is used when leaving an assigned room such as a study room, dorm, hotel or exam hall, and its opposite is '입실하다'. At hotels people more often say '체크아웃하다'. When leaving a hospital, you use '퇴원하다' instead.

examples.en: The proposal I submitted was rejected by my team leader.
Mother rejected the clothes, saying they were too big.

examples.ko: 그 사람한테 데이트 신청했다가 퇴짜 맞았어요.
examples.en: I asked him out and got turned down.
I'm upset because I was turned down three times.

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 불량품이라며 물건에 퇴짜를 놨어요.
examples.en: The shop owner rejected the goods, saying they were defective.
What should I do if it gets rejected again?

explain: 제안, 물건, 고백 같은 것을 받아 주지 않고 거절하는 일이에요. 거절하는 쪽은 '퇴짜를 놓다', 거절당하는 쪽은 '퇴짜를 맞다'(또는 '퇴짜 당하다')라고 해요. 조금 구어체이고, 딱딱한 말로는 '거절', '반려'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is rejecting a proposal, item or confession instead of accepting it. The one who rejects says '퇴짜를 놓다', and the one rejected says '퇴짜를 맞다'. It is somewhat colloquial, and more formal words are '거절' and '반려'.

examples.ko: 저희는 어제부터 이 호텔에 투숙하고 있어요.
examples.en: We have been staying at this hotel since yesterday.
Please show your passport when you check in.
I stayed two nights in Busan for a business trip.
That celebrity is staying at our hotel.

examples.ko: 투숙한 손님은 조식을 무료로 드실 수 있어요.
examples.en: Guests who stay here can have breakfast for free.

examples.ko: 가족과 함께 바닷가 근처 펜션에 투숙할 거예요.
examples.en: I will stay with my family at a pension near the beach.

explain: 호텔, 여관, 펜션 같은 숙박 시설에 돈을 내고 묵는 것을 말하는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '묵다'나 '자다'를 더 많이 하고, '투숙하다'는 호텔 직원의 안내나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 방을 비울 때는 '퇴실하다'나 '체크아웃하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat formal word for paying to stay at lodging such as a hotel, inn or pension. In daily life people say '묵다' or '자다' more, while '투숙하다' appears in hotel staff announcements and news. When leaving, you use '퇴실하다' or '체크아웃하다'.

examples.ko: 투표용지에 두 명을 표시하면 그 표는 무효예요.
examples.en: If you mark two people on the ballot paper, that vote is invalid.
At the polling station, I first received a ballot paper.
There weren't enough ballot papers, so people waited.
I folded the ballot paper and put it in the ballot box.

examples.ko: 학급 회장 선거 투표용지에 이름을 적었어요.
examples.en: I wrote a name on the ballot paper for the class president election.

examples.ko: 잘못 찍은 투표용지는 바꿔 주지 않아요.
examples.en: They don't replace a ballot paper that was marked wrong.

explain: 선거나 투표 때 후보나 의견을 표시하는 종이예요. 보통 '투표용지를 받다/기표하다/넣다'처럼 말해요. 학교 회장 선거에서도 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '투표지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: This is the paper on which you mark a candidate or opinion during an election or vote. It's usually used as '투표용지를 받다/기표하다/넣다'. It's used in school president elections too, and the news also says '투표지'.

examples.ko: 여론 조사에서는 앞섰지만 실제 당선 여부는 투표함을 열어 봐야 알아요.
examples.en: He led in the polls, but we can only know if he really wins once the ballot box is opened.

examples.ko: 투표함을 열기 전까지 가결 여부는 아무도 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Until the ballot box was opened, nobody could know whether it would pass.
I put my ballot in the ballot box and came out.
When voting ended, they moved the ballot boxes to the counting hall.

examples.ko: 투표함 앞에 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
examples.en: People are lined up in front of the ballot box.
We made a simple ballot box in the classroom.

explain: 투표용지를 넣는 상자예요. 뉴스에서 '투표함을 열어 봐야 안다'처럼 결과를 알기 전까지는 모른다는 뜻으로도 자주 말해요. 개표는 '투표함을 열고 표를 세는 일'이에요.
explain_en: This is the box where ballots are put. In the news, 'we have to open the ballot box to know' is often used to mean you can't know the result until it's counted. '개표' is opening the box and counting the votes.

examples.en: My little brother grumbles that he doesn't want to clean.
He grumbled every morning about getting up early.
Stop grumbling and help me a bit.
Father grumbled, but in the end he drove me there.
My friend was grumbling something to himself.

examples.ko: 툴툴거리지 말고 하고 싶은 말을 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't mutter; say what you want to say.

explain: '투덜거리다'와 비슷하지만 목소리를 낮게 깔고 퉁명스럽게 불평하는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '~다고 툴툴거리다'처럼 쓰고, 불평하면서도 결국 할 일은 하는 사람에게 자주 써요. 큰 소리로 따지는 '항의하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is similar to '투덜거리다' but has a stronger feel of grumbling bluntly in a low voice. It is usually used like '~다고 툴툴거리다', often for someone who complains but ends up doing the job anyway. It differs from '항의하다', which is protesting loudly.

examples.ko: 직원의 대답이 너무 퉁명스러워서 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: The staff member's answer was so curt that I felt bad.
That friend's way of speaking is a bit blunt.

examples.ko: 아버지는 퉁명스럽게 대답하셨지만 속은 따뜻한 분이에요.
examples.en: Father answered bluntly, but he's warm inside.
Why are you so curt today of all days?
He answered the phone in a curt voice.
I'm sorry for being so blunt.

explain: 말이나 행동이 친절하지 않고 무뚝뚝해서 듣는 사람이 서운할 수 있는 모습이에요. 화가 나서 그런 것일 수도, 그냥 성격일 수도 있어요. ㅂ불규칙이라서 '퉁명스러워요', '퉁명스러운'으로 바뀌고, 보통 '말투/대답/목소리'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes words or behavior that are unfriendly and brusque, which can hurt the listener's feelings. It might be from anger or just personality. It's a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes '퉁명스러워요' and '퉁명스러운', and it usually goes with '말투', '대답' or '목소리'.

examples.en: In spring I often wear a thin trench coat.
It was raining, so I went out wearing a trench coat.
This trench coat has a belt at the waist.
For trench coats, beige is the most popular color.
I bought a trench coat to wear in autumn.
If you wear a knit under a trench coat, you stay warm.

explain: 허리에 벨트가 있고 길이가 긴 얇은 겉옷이에요. 한국에서는 봄과 가을에 많이 입어서 '환절기 코트'라는 느낌이 있어요. 겨울 코트처럼 두껍지 않아서 '코트'와 따로 이야기하기도 해요.
explain_en: It's a thin, long outer coat with a belt at the waist. In Korea it's worn a lot in spring and autumn, so it has the feel of a 'between-seasons coat'. Since it isn't thick like a winter coat, people often talk about it separately from a regular '코트'.

examples.en: My mom's cooking skill is something special.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 고집이 특별나서 말을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: That child is unusually stubborn, so he doesn't listen well.
There's no particular reason for it.
My town is known for being exceptionally warm-hearted.
Grandfather's love for his grandchildren is exceptional.
There's no need to act so peculiar.

explain: 다른 것과 비교해서 눈에 띄게 다르거나 유난하다는 느낌이에요. '특별하다'보다 구어체이고, 때로는 좀 유난스럽다는 뉘앙스도 있어요. '특별난 이유가 없다'처럼 부정문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of being noticeably different or out of the ordinary. It is more colloquial than '특별하다' and sometimes has a nuance of being a bit over the top. It often appears in negatives like '특별난 이유가 없다'.

examples.ko: 작은 회사는 틈새시장을 노리는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good for a small company to aim for a niche market.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 틈새시장을 잘 찾아서 성공했어요.
examples.en: This shop succeeded by finding a good niche market.

examples.ko: 반려동물 용품이 새로운 틈새시장으로 주목받고 있어요.
examples.en: Pet supplies are getting attention as a new niche market.

examples.ko: 큰 회사가 놓친 틈새시장에서 기회를 찾았어요.
examples.en: We found an opportunity in a niche market that big companies missed.

examples.ko: 틈새시장은 경쟁이 적은 대신 손님도 적어요.
examples.en: A niche market has less competition but also fewer customers.

examples.ko: 저는 틈새시장을 공략하는 창업을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm preparing a startup that targets a niche market.

explain: 큰 회사들이 잘 다루지 않는 작고 특별한 수요를 가진 시장이에요. 뉴스나 창업, 경제 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '틈새시장을 노리다/공략하다/찾다'처럼 써요. '틈새'가 '좁은 빈틈'이라는 말이라 큰 시장 사이의 빈틈이라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It's a market with small, special demand that big companies don't handle well. It often appears in news, startup and economy talk, used as '틈새시장을 노리다/공략하다/찾다'. Since '틈새' means a narrow gap, it feels like a gap between large markets.

examples.ko: 새 신발을 신었더니 발에 티눈이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After wearing new shoes, I got a corn on my foot.
Because of the corn, it hurts every time I walk.
I had the corn removed at the hospital.
The corn on my toe is getting bigger and bigger.

examples.ko: 꽉 끼는 구두는 티눈의 원인이 돼요.
examples.en: Tight dress shoes can be a cause of corns.
It hurts less after putting on a corn pad.

explain: 신발에 계속 눌리거나 쓸려서 발가락이나 발바닥 피부가 단단하게 굳은 것이에요. 가운데 심이 박혀 있어서 누르면 아프고, 그냥 굳은살과는 달라요. 보통 '티눈이 생기다/박히다', '티눈을 빼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It's a hardened spot of skin on the toes or soles caused by constant pressure or rubbing from shoes. It has a core in the middle that hurts when pressed, so it differs from a plain callus. People usually say '티눈이 생기다/박히다' and '티눈을 빼다'.
